That’s basically still me in grad school—I feel like my brain is running five tabs at once, words tumble out quickly, and I get distracted mid-sentence. I pace when I’m studying, tap my foot nonstop in seminars, and I hate just sitting still; I always feel like I have to be doing something.

Sleep has never really felt essential. Since I was little, I’d be up late reading or working on projects and still wake up early, feeling oddly okay on just a few hours. It’s not like a switch flips on and off; this is just my baseline.

Over the last year or so, though, I’ve also been really down. I don’t enjoy things I used to, even hanging out with friends feels flat. I’m exhausted all the time, even though my body still won’t sit still—I pace, pick at my skin, fidget constantly. I cry over small things and my coursework has taken a hit because I can’t seem to find the energy to actually follow through.
D009-D003_h022.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D009-D003_h023.question:
I’ve always been kind of “on,” even as a kid. My parents used to get calls from teachers because I couldn’t sit still, talked way too fast, and would blurt things out or jump from one thing to another. That’s pretty much been my baseline my whole life—racing thoughts, talking quickly, bouncing between tasks, staying up late because my mind just won’t shut off, but somehow still feeling okay in the morning.

The last year or so, though, I’ve felt really down. It’s like someone turned the volume way down on me internally but left the restlessness. I have almost no drive to plan lessons or grade; I put things off until the last minute. Even walking down the hallway feels slower, like I’m moving through molasses, and thinking through a new lesson exhausts me after a few minutes. My mood’s been pretty low most days for over a year.

About three months ago, I had a stretch where my mood swung around more—sometimes oddly upbeat and then suddenly irritable. I was piling on extra projects at school and barely sleeping, maybe three or four hours, but still feeling wired rather than tired. But honestly, that fast-talking, jumpy, distractible feeling isn’t new—it’s been there since elementary school; it just kind of ramped up.
D009-D003_h023.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D009-D003_h024.question:
I’ve always been kind of “too much,” even as a kid. Teachers would complain I talked nonstop, jumped from one thing to another, couldn’t sit still, and my mind was always racing. That hasn’t really changed. My coworkers joke that I’m like a hummingbird on espresso—I’m constantly pacing around the shop, starting five tasks at once, talking really fast, cutting people off without meaning to. It’s like my thoughts are going faster than my mouth can keep up with.

I don’t really feel like I need much sleep. Since I was little I’ve stayed up late, just buzzing with ideas, reorganizing things, scrolling, planning new displays for the store, then I’m up early again. I don’t actually feel tired at night; sleep feels optional until my body just crashes.

The last year or so, though, I’ve also had these long stretches where I feel like I’m moving through mud. My body feels heavy, even walking around the store is exhausting, and I’ve been avoiding friends and dating. I just feel flat inside, like my emotions are muted. It’s made it hard to keep up with work and my social life, even though my mind still won’t slow down.
D009-D003_h024.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)

D009-D003_h025.question:
I’ve always been “go go go” since I was a kid. My mom used to say I was like a wind‑up toy that never ran down. Even back in elementary school I talked fast, jumped from one thing to another, and could stay up half the night reading or drawing and still be buzzing the next day. That’s kind of just…stayed the same into adulthood. I’m constantly fidgeting at the clinic, pacing between rooms, starting one task and then another before I finish the first. My brain feels like it’s got ten radio stations on at once—racing thoughts, jumping topics, and I talk so quickly my coworkers ask me to slow down. I honestly don’t feel like I ever really need much sleep; I fight going to bed and then wake up wired.

Over the last year or so, though, it’s like I hit a wall. I stopped caring about the stuff I used to love—trail running, baking, even playing with my dog. I move slower, even just walking down the hall, and simple things feel like wading through mud. I’m exhausted all the time even when I sleep enough, and I’ve had days where I just start crying at work for no obvious reason. That’s been messing with my job and my social life a lot.
D009-D003_h025.options:
A. Adjustment Disorder
    B. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    C. Bipolar II Disorder
    D. Attention-Deficit/Hyperactivity Disorder (Predominantly Hyperactive/Impulsive Presentation)
